stories.headline: TRUMP REJECTS IRAN PEACE PROPOSAL AS "TOTALLY UNACCEPTABLE", HORMUZ CLOSURE DRAGS INTO WEEK 11
stories.body: President Trump dismissed Iran's latest ceasefire response Monday, prolonging the effective closure of the Strait of Hormuz that has choked roughly 21% of global oil supply since late February. Brent crude surged to $104.80/bbl (+3.5%) while WTI climbed near $99 — keeping inflation fears elevated heading into Thursday's CPI print. Stocks held near records despite the spike, reflecting market confidence the Fed won't respond to supply-side inflation with rate hikes.

stories.headline: S&P 500 CLOSES AT 7,417 AS MARKETS ABSORB OIL SHOCK; THURSDAY CPI NOW KEY CATALYST
stories.body: Equities finished modestly higher Monday — S&P +0.24%, Nasdaq +0.13%, Dow +0.07% to 49,642 — as traders balanced the oil surge against a lack of broader risk-off selling. The resilience reflects a market pricing in Fed patience, but that bet faces its first real stress test Thursday when April CPI prints. The Hormuz closure is now 10+ weeks old, long enough for energy cost pass-through to show up in core services inflation.

stories.headline: BRENT ABOVE $104 AS HORMUZ PREMIUM SURGES; QATARI LNG DISRUPTION PUSHES EUROPEAN GAS TO $38/MMBTU
stories.body: WTI climbed near $99/bbl Monday (+3.2%), with Brent at $104.80 (+3.5%), as the Hormuz closure eliminates alternative routing for Gulf producers. The LNG side is equally acute: Qatari exports — roughly 80 million tonnes per year, all transiting Hormuz — remain curtailed, driving European TTF gas to $38/MMBtu and amplifying the global inflation impulse beyond just crude. Gold slipped 0.36% to $4,699 despite the geopolitical flare-up.

stories.headline: US-CHINA 30% TARIFF TRUCE HOLDS THROUGH NOV 2026; CHINA EXPORTS TO US DOWN 16% IN Q1
stories.body: The November 2025 tariff reduction agreement keeps US tariffs on Chinese goods at 30% through November 2026, but the economic drag is visible: China's exports to the US fell 16% in Q1 2026 year-on-year, while total Chinese exports grew 14% to $977.6 billion in Q1 — trade diversion, not pure demand destruction. The White House's Board of Trade is reportedly exploring a managed-trade framework using sectoral tariff approvals as a longer-term mechanism.

stories.headline: NCAA EXPANDS MARCH MADNESS TO 76 TEAMS STARTING 2027; "FIRST FOUR" REPLACED BY 12-GAME OPENING ROUND
stories.body: The NCAA Division I men's and women's basketball committees voted Thursday to expand the tournament from 68 to 76 teams, effective 2027. The "First Four" is abolished and replaced by a 12-game opening round played over two days the week after Selection Sunday, with 12 winners advancing to create a 64-team bracket. The NCAA projects the expansion will distribute more than $131 million in additional revenue to member schools over the remaining six years of current broadcast agreements.

stories.headline: KNICKS SWEEP 76ERS TO REACH SECOND STRAIGHT EASTERN CONFERENCE FINALS; TIE PLAYOFF 3-PT RECORD
stories.body: New York punched its ticket to back-to-back conference finals with a dominant Game 4 blowout over Philadelphia, drilling a playoff-record-tying 25 three-pointers in a 30-point win. In the West, OKC is one win from sweeping the Lakers (leads 3-0), extending the defending champs' unbeaten playoff run. Detroit leads Cleveland 2-1 in the other Eastern semifinal with Game 4 at Rocket Arena tonight (8 PM ET).

stories.headline: NFL SCHEDULE RELEASE THURSDAY MAY 14; OTAS BEGIN LEAGUE-WIDE AS OFFSEASON ROSTER MOVES SETTLE
stories.body: All 32 teams open voluntary OTA workouts this week, with the full 2026 schedule unveiled Thursday at 5 PM PT on NFL Network and ESPN2. Seahawks fans get the first look at the Super Bowl champs' title-defense slate. Notable settled moves: Trey Hendrickson to Baltimore (4yr/$112M, $60M guaranteed), Kenneth Walker III re-signed in Seattle (3yr/$45M), and the Chiefs acquired QB Justin Fields from the Jets for a 2027 sixth-round pick.

stories.headline: 2026 TRANSFER PORTAL WINDOW CLOSED; LSU TOPS NATIONAL CLASS WITH QB SAM LEAVITT FROM USC
stories.body: The 15-day transfer portal window is closed with LSU holding the consensus No. 1 portal class, headlined by five-star QB Sam Leavitt from USC. Penn State's new coaching staff assembled a class approaching 40 transfers. At Washington, head coach Jedd Fisch wrapped spring ball with the Dawgs After Dark game (Purple 27, Gold 10) and will call plays himself in 2026 after OC Jimmie Dougherty departed in February.

deepDive.title: Hormuz Premium: How a Shipping Chokepoint Rewires the Inflation Outlook
content: Trump's rejection of Iran's latest ceasefire proposal today kept WTI near $99 and Brent above $104 — levels the market has been absorbing since Iran effectively closed the Strait of Hormuz in late February. The surface read is a commodity story. The deeper read is a monetary policy story. A quarter of global oil and roughly 20% of all LNG transit a 21-mile-wide channel daily. When that channel closes, the price impact is disproportionate to the lost volume because energy derivatives, tanker routing, and supply chains are all calibrated around Hormuz being open.

The mechanism works in two waves. The first is the 'Hormuz premium' in crude: tankers that normally deliver Saudi, Iraqi, and UAE crude to Asia must reroute around the Cape of Good Hope, adding 15–18 transit days and $4–6/bbl in freight costs. Options markets price a probability-weighted disruption risk into the front-month contract, flattening backwardation and signaling scarcity to global refiners. The second wave is product cracks — gasoline, diesel, jet fuel — that widen 6–8 weeks after the crude spike and feed directly into transportation costs, a major input to core services inflation. That second-wave pass-through is precisely what Thursday's CPI print will begin to capture.

What gets missed in equity coverage is the LNG transmission. Qatar, the world's largest LNG exporter at roughly 80 million tonnes per year, ships exclusively through Hormuz. European buyers relying on Qatari top-up cargoes have been forced to bid aggressively for US Gulf Coast LNG spot cargoes, pushing Henry Hub prices 40% higher and JKM (the Asia LNG benchmark) to $41/MMBtu. European TTF gas is now at $38/MMBtu, feeding into manufacturing and electricity costs across the continent. The closest historical analogy is 1979: the Iranian Revolution removed 2.5 mbpd and drove US core CPI from 6% to 13% over 18 months, ultimately forcing the Volcker Fed to a 20% funds rate. Today's disruption is larger in absolute barrels at risk, though energy mix diversification provides some buffer.

The Fed's posture — treat this as a transitory supply-side shock, not demand-pull inflation — is the central assumption holding equity multiples near record levels. If Thursday's CPI shows core above +0.4% MoM, that assumption gets challenged: fed funds futures will reprice hawkish holds or hikes, the 2s10s spread will steepen, and equity multiples will compress. The S&P's flat reaction today signals traders aren't pricing that as the base case. But Thursday is the first CPI that fully captures the Hormuz cost pass-through into services, making it the most consequential print in months. For a market at all-time highs with oil near $99 and the Strait still closed, it's the number that matters.
